name: lsasecrets
description: LSA secrets: survey the policy's secret store and read its values in place -- the inventory enumerated out of the registry's SECURITY subtree, the values asked back through the LSA's policy API (the system performs its own decryption), nothing landing on disk -- collect.lsasecrets's execution half packed as the artifact an implant loads through module.load.

opsec.notes: Server side, the package lands as descriptor rows and one artifact file under the module store -- no code runs in the teamserver. On the target, the implant half loads from staged task content and nothing it does lands on disk: the subtree and the values are read where they sit, in the implant process's own LSA session, and the rows ride the task's channel back. Both halves of the act answer to the SYSTEM seat -- the subtree that enumerates the names answers SYSTEM alone, and so do the secret objects the policy API queries -- so an implant that is merely elevated refuses once, named. The values are the store's own secrets (service-account passwords, the auto-logon password, the DPAPI machine keys, the machine-account password) in plain reach of the audit log the rows enter. The verb rides the per-engagement module load -- never a default profile.
